verse1.philosophical_explanation: Bhagavad Gita Chapter 6 Verse 1 offers a layered teaching on disciplined action, inner clarity, and God-centered wisdom, presenting dharma as a harmonizing principle that integrates duty, knowledge, devotion, and self-mastery. The text therefore asks the reader to cultivate viveka, sustained discrimination between the permanent and the impermanent, while remaining active in righteous responsibilities. It also emphasizes that true strength is not aggression but alignment with satya, ahimsa in intent, self-restraint, and surrender to the Divine will. Ethical life in Sanatana Dharma emerges through disciplined action offered without egoic possessiveness, where one performs svadharma with humility and accountability. This teaching is socially relevant because it links personal transformation with collective order: families, communities, and governance remain stable only when conduct is rooted in justice, gratitude, and reverence for truth. Spiritually, the section invites bhakti and contemplative awareness, showing that liberation-oriented living can begin within ordinary duties when the heart is purified through right understanding and service.
verse1.scripture_text: श्रीभगवानुवाच | अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः | स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ||६-१||

verse.sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः | स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ||६-१||
verse.translation: 6.1 The Blessed Lord said He who performs his bounden duty without depending on the fruits of his actions he is a Sannyasi and a Yogi; not he who is without fire and without action.
verse.transliteration: śrībhagavānuvāca . anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ . sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ ||6-1||

verse.translation: 6.11 In a clean spot, having established a firm seat of his own, neither too high nor too low, made of a cloth, a skin and Kusa-grass, one over the other.
verse.transliteration: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ . nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram ||6-11||

verse.translation: 6.12 There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and the senses controlled, let him, seated on the seat, practise Yoga for the purification of the self.
verse.transliteration: tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ . upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye ||6-12||

verse.translation: 6.13 Let him firmly hold his body, head and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of his nose, without looking around.
verse.transliteration: samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ . samprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan ||6-13||

verse.translation: 6.14 Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of a Brahmachari, having controlled the mind, thinking of Me and balanced in mind, let him sit, having Me as his supreme goal.
verse.transliteration: praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ . manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ ||6-14||

verse.translation: 6.15 Thus always keeping the mind balanced, the Yogi, with the mind controlled, attains to the peace abiding in Me, which culminates in liberation.
verse.transliteration: yuñjannevaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ . śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthāmadhigacchati ||6-15||
